[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Evolution of Classic Deep Learning Architectures"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"The journey of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) has been defined by the pursuit of deeper and more efficient networks. In this tutorial, we will explore four landmark architectures that shaped computer vision: VGG, ResNet, DenseNet, and EfficientNet."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. VGG: Simplicity and Uniformity"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Introduced by the Visual Geometry Group at Oxford, VGG demonstrated that network depth is critical for good accuracy. VGG-16 and VGG-19 replaced large convolution filters with multiple stacked 3x3 filters."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Utilizes very small receptive fields (3x3) stacked together to mimic larger filters."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"High memory consumption and massive parameter count due to fully connected layers."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"2. ResNet: Residual Learning and Skipping Connections"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"As networks grew deeper, the vanishing gradient problem hindered training. ResNet solved this by introducing shortcut connections (skip connections) that add the input of a layer to its output."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class ResidualBlock(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, channels):
        super(ResidualBlock, self).__init__()
        self.conv1 = nn.Conv2d(channels, channels, kernel_size=3, padding=1)
        self.relu = nn.ReLU()
        self.conv2 = nn.Conv2d(channels, channels, kernel_size=3, padding=1)

    def forward(self, x):
        residual = x
        out = self.relu(self.conv1(x))
        out = self.conv2(out)
        out += residual
        return self.relu(out)"},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"3. DenseNet: Feature Reuse via Dense Connectivity"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"DenseNet (Densely Connected Convolutional Networks) takes the skip connection concept further. In a dense block, every layer receives the feature maps of all preceding layers as input, maximizing information flow."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Alleviates the vanishing gradient problem significantly."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Extremely parameter-efficient due to direct feature concatenation."},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"4. EfficientNet: Principled Network Scaling"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"Rather than arbitrarily scaling depth, width, or resolution, EfficientNet uses a compound coefficient to uniformly scale all three dimensions in a balanced way using Neural Architecture Search (NAS)."},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"# Example concept of loading a pretrained EfficientNet using torchvision
from torchvision.models import efficientnet_b0, EfficientNet_B0_Weights

weights = EfficientNet_B0_Weights.DEFAULT
model = efficientnet_b0(weights=weights)
model.eval()
print("EfficientNet-B0 loaded successfully for inference.")"},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"Understanding these classic architectures provides a solid foundation for modern computer vision. VGG teaches us about structural depth, ResNet about gradient flow, DenseNet about feature reuse, and EfficientNet about optimal resource scaling."}]
